subject: Proposal: term amendment impact & capacity uplift pathway
messages:
From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@dataforge.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@dataforge.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Term amendment impact & capacity uplift

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the Q1 consumption summary you sent earlier. Our leadership wants to evaluate a short mid‑term amendment to our existing contract so we can bring forward additional committed capacity for the next six months. Before procurement drafts anything, can you confirm: 

- A breakdown of token spend by usage type (completions vs embeddings vs reranks) for Jan–Mar 2028;
- Whether any recent runtime changes (quantization/batching) materially change unit economics; and
- A recommended uplift (relative to current commit) that balances cost and headroom for our peak traffic.

Vikram (engineering) and procurement are looped in — they’ll need the ROI numbers for our execs. Fast turnaround appreciated, we’re trying to close internal approval this week.

Best,
Aisha
Director, Product
DataForge Labs
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@dataforge.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Term amendment impact & capacity uplift

Aisha — thanks, attached the CSV (DF_consumption_Q1_2028.csv) and a short runtime efficiency writeup (runtime_efficiency_report.pdf). High level answers below; details in the attachment.

Quick summary (Jan–Mar 2028):
- Token mix: ~58% generation/completions, ~32% embeddings, ~10% reranking/other.
- Unit cost trend: 12% lower effective cost per inference token since Feb after enabling adaptive batching + prefix KV cache for 60% of requests.
- Latency: p50 unchanged; p95 tail improved ~9% on the new batching profile but may show variance on very short (<8 token) completion requests.

Recommendation for uplift: propose a 10% uplift to current committed monthly tokens with a 6‑month amendment and a one‑time credit to offset migration/ops effort. Rationale: expected to cover peak delta while preserving volume discounts; with the recommended quantization profile we estimate a net per‑token savings of ~7–9% vs current run rate.

Next steps I propose:
1) Monica to validate the runtime savings assumption (technical note attached).
2) We’ll share a redline of the amendment for procurement to review (proposed_term_amendment_redline.docx).
3) If DataForge wants a larger uplift (15–20%), we can model a stepped commit that phases in extra capacity over two months to reduce immediate spend.

Attaching: DF_consumption_Q1_2028.csv; runtime_efficiency_report.pdf; proposed_term_amendment_redline.docx

—
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555‑0134
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@dataforge.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 13:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Term amendment impact & capacity uplift — technical note

On Tue, Mar 20, 2028 at 11:03 AM rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai wrote:
> Aisha — thanks, attached the CSV (DF_consumption_Q1_2028.csv) and a short runtime efficiency writeup (runtime_efficiency_report.pdf). High level answers below; details in the attachment.

Quick technical addendum from ops/CS: 
- Verified the ~12% effective unit cost improvement; breakdown: 6.5% from adaptive batching (workload alignment), 3% from prefix KV cache hit rate (~18% overall), 2.5% from switching selected heavy‑tail models to int8 quantization on dedicated pools.
- Risk: if DataForge shifts to many sub‑8 token completions in high volume, batching benefits drop quickly — we recommend enabling small‑request pooling for that segment (we can do this with minimal config).
- Expected perf delta with proposed profile: net 7–9% unit cost reduction + p95 tail improvement of ~9%.

If procurement needs tighter bounds for exec review, we can run a 48‑hour experimental traffic replay against a mirror pool and share the result; that typically takes 2–3 business days to schedule.

—
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@dataforge.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Vikram Rao <vikram@dataforge.com>, procurement@dataforge.com
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 08:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Term amendment impact & capacity uplift

Thanks Rishi/Monica — this is helpful. Procurement wants the amendment redline and the numeric ROI in a single slide for our execs. Two clarifications before we proceed: 

1) You recommend 10% uplift — we are targeting a 20% uplift if the economics support it; can you run a delta model showing 10% vs 20% committed uplift (net savings, expected credits, and worst‑case spend)?
2) How will the proposed change affect our SLA (p95 latency and throughput guarantees) — and can we include a short fallback policy (e.g., fall back to a slightly cheaper model family during extreme load with guaranteed correctness bounds)?

Also procurement asked if you can send the redline in a track‑changes friendly format; they prefer Docx. We received the Docx you attached and will circulate it internally.

Vikram — for the replay test Monica mentioned, are there specific traffic segments you want mirrored?

Best,
Aisha
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.kapoor@dataforge.com>, procurement@dataforge.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Term amendment impact & capacity uplift — next steps and timelines

Aisha — appreciate the quick feedback. Summary of agreed next steps and timeline: 

1) Modeling: We will send a simple delta model (10% vs 20%) with three scenarios (expected, conservative, worst case) by Mon, Mar 27 COB. That will include net per‑token savings and projected monthly spend under the amendment.
2) SLA & fallback: Kimberly will draft a fallback policy that pins a compatible model family with documented output parity thresholds. That doc will be ready by Tue, Mar 28. SLA p95 commitments remain unchanged for the amendment; fallback only applies when utilization exceeds emergency thresholds and will be opt‑in.
3) Replay test: Vikram/DF choose representative traffic segments (we recommend 1) interactive chat flows, 2) embeddings bulk batch, 3) short completions under 8 tokens). Monica will schedule the 48‑hour replay on Wed/Thu next week once Vikram confirms segments.
4) Legal/redline: I’ll upload a clean DocuSign version of the amendment once procurement gives a green light; internal legal has preapproved the proposed credits structure.

Owner matrix: modeling (Rishi), technical validation & replay (Monica + Ops), SLA/fallback doc (Kimberly), procurement/contract (Aisha/Vikram).

Links: HubSpot deal DF-2028-042 (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DF-2028-042) and the draft redline I uploaded here: https://www.docusign.com/link/DF-2028-042-sign.

If that aligns I’ll put the amendment into DocuSign and tag procurement for signature.

Thanks —
Rishi
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
